summary: Iteration_174 verification: validated FIX A (routers/review.py sign_off() smarter fallback priority) and FIX B (migrations/m039_fix_sign_off_manager_admin_misattribution) end-to-end. Extended /app/backend/tests/test_portfolio_signoff_fix.py from 6 to 11 tests — all 11 pass. New tests cover: (a) admin signs off a meeting with exactly one manager-role attendee -> that manager is credited, NOT the admin (the exact production scenario the user reported); (b) admin signs off with 2+ ambiguous manager/admin attendees -> sign_off_manager_id stays NULL (don't guess); (c) manager self-signoff with themselves as sole manager attendee -> self-credited (common case regression); (d) schema_migrations ledger confirms '039_fix_sign_off_manager_admin_misattribution' is applied in preview; (e) m039 SQL re-run against 3 synthetic rows correctly fixes admin-misattribution rows while leaving legit admin-conducted rows AND already-correct manager-attributed rows untouched. One existing iter_173 test (test_signoff_backfills_null_sign_off_manager_id) had its EXPECTED result updated from 'admin gets credited' to 'stays NULL' — the test's own scenario (admin+manager both as attendees, admin signs) is now the ambiguous-admin case that FIX A deliberately leaves NULL rather than mis-attributing; this is the correct new behavior, not a regression. Added resilient login helper (retries 429/5xx with backoff) to the test file to survive rate-limit flakiness.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/review.py sign_off() fallback priority is well-structured and matches the comment contract: (1) prefer existing sign_off_manager_id (unchanged), (2) prefer unambiguous single manager/admin attendee (ground-truth composition), (3) only when ambiguous AND signer is non-admin, fall back to signer, (4) ambiguous AND admin signer => leave NULL. Code also preserves COALESCE on UPDATE, so even the fallback cannot overwrite an already-assigned supervisor.

m039 SQL uses a CTE with correct NULL-safe aggregation, joins on users.id = sign_off_manager_id AND u.role='admin' AND u.org_id=m.org_id, requires exactly one manager-role attendee differing from the current admin, and regex-guards the UUID extract — matches the described conservative scope. Verified empirically against synthetic Case B (admin is sole manager-role) and Case C (already-correct manager) that neither is touched.

m039 is correctly registered in both the import and MIGRATIONS list in migrations/__init__.py and the ledger shows applied_at = 2026-10-17 13:53:19 UTC (0 rows affected in preview — expected, as preview's current data doesn't match the exact production-only mis-attribution pattern).

If preview starts 502-ing during login during test runs, that's K8s ingress rate-limiting between parallel xdist workers — the helper now retries with backoff; running with `-n 0` (serial) is also safe. rca of the issue: iteration_173 shipped m037/m038 which backfilled sign_off_manager_id using sign_off_record->>'signed_by'. That is 'whoever clicked the sign-off button', not necessarily the conducting supervisor. For meetings signed off by an ADMIN on behalf of someone else (admin role allowed to sign off per sign_off()'s role check), m037/m038 mis-attributed the meeting TO the admin instead of the real manager attendee. Portfolio exclusion filter (`sign_off_manager_id IS NULL OR != caller_id`) then kept these meetings visible in the real conducting manager's own My Portfolio (since the ID pointed at the admin, not them). FIX A rewrote sign_off()'s fallback priority to prefer the unambiguous manager/admin attendee over 'whoever clicked', and refuses to guess when ambiguous AND signer is admin. FIX B (m039) corrects already-written mis-attributions in-place for rows where exactly one manager-role attendee exists and differs from the admin currently credited. Verified via SQL re-run on 3 synthetic rows (correction case + 2 no-op cases) — all three post-conditions correct.
